title: Marie Curie: Radioactivity Pioneer
description: The first woman to win a Nobel Prize, who discovered radium and polonium while revolutionizing science
imageHint: ☢️ Glowing discoveries that changed physics and chemistry ⚛️

questions.question: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. In which scientific field did she win her first one?
questions.hint: The science of matter, energy, and their interactions - not chemistry

questions.question: What radioactive element did Marie Curie discover and name after her homeland?
questions.hint: Named after Poland, where she was born, it's element 84 on the periodic table

questions.question: Marie Curie coined which term to describe the emission of rays from uranium and other elements?
questions.hint: The property of certain elements to emit energy in the form of rays or particles

questions.question: During World War I, Marie Curie developed mobile X-ray units. What were these vehicles nicknamed?
questions.hint: They were called 'little' versions of her name in French

questions.question: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields. Chemistry was her second - what was her groundbreaking work there?
questions.hint: She successfully isolated a pure sample of this glowing element

deeperMode.title: Radium's Deadly Glow
deeperMode.description: The dangerous beauty of radioactivity and its ultimate cost to the pioneering scientist

questions.question: Marie Curie's laboratory notebooks are still radioactive today. How many years will they remain dangerous?
questions.hint: More than a millennium and a half - they're kept in lead-lined boxes in Paris

questions.question: What ultimately caused Marie Curie's death, likely from years of radiation exposure?
questions.hint: A blood disorder where the bone marrow stops producing enough blood cells
